''Senecio exsquameus'' Brot.{{cite web | url = http://ww2.bgbm.org/EuroPlusMed/PTaxonDetail.asp?NameId=7000688&PTRefFk=7000000 | title = Details for: ''Senecio gallicus'' | access-date = 2008-04-22 |author1=Botanic Garden | author-link = Botanical Garden in Berlin |author2=Botanical Museum Berlin-Dahlem |name-list-style=amp | work = Euro+Med PlantBase | publisher = [[Free University of Berlin|Freie Universität Berlin]] }} }} '''''Senecio gallicus''''', an [[annual plant]] of the genus ''[[Senecio]]'' and family [[Asteraceae]], is a species that colonizes isolated habitats with [[Natural Stress|difficult]] environmental conditions. It is widespread across [[southern France]] and the [[Iberian Peninsula]] in [[desert]]s and [[Deserts and xeric shrublands|xeric shrublands]], on [[steppe]]s and salty dry [[coastal plain]]s. ''S. gallicus'' is playing a predominant role in shaping patterns of genetic structure by presenting models of [[Population ecology|historical associations among population]] rather than patterns of ongoing gene flow.{{cite journal | last =Thompson | first =John D | title =Population differentiation in Mediterranean plants: insights into colonization history and the evolution and conservation of endemic species | journal =[[Heredity (journal)|Heredity]] | volume =82 | issue =3 | pages =229–236 | date =March 1999 | doi =10.1038/sj.hdy.6885040 | pmid =10336696 | doi-access =free }} ==Common names== *{{langx|en|French groundsel}}{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }} *{{langx|es|Azuzón de Alborán}} *{{langx|fr|Séneçon de France}} *{{langx|it|Senecione gallico}} ==Description== ''Senecio gallicus'' has had more [[Phylogenetics|phylogenetic]] description because it is an exceptional species among [[Halotolerance|halotypes]] with a known intraspecific [[Phylogeography|phylogeographic]] structure which is also species specific.{{cite journal | last =Comes | first =Hans Peter |author2=Richard J. Abbott | journal =[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]] | volume = 55 | issue = 10 | pages =1943–1962 | date =October 2001 | doi =10.1554/0014-3820(2001)055[1943:MPRALS]2.0.CO;2 | issn =0014-3820 | pmid=11761056| title =Molecular Phylogeography, Reticulation, and Lineage Sorting in Mediterranean Senecio Sect. Senecio (Asteraceae) }} Comparisons of [[allozyme]] and [[chloroplast]] variation in this species indicate that it persisted in [[Pleistocene]] coastal [[Refugium (population biology)|refugia]] during [[Glacial period|glaciation periods]]. ;The Endangered One: '''''Senecio alboranicus''''', or '''azuzón de Alborán''', is reported to be [[Endemism|endemic]] to and [[Critically endangered species|critically endangered]] on [[Isla de Alborán]] by [[IUCN Red List|ICUN]]. Alborán is 7.1 [[hectares]]{{cite iucn |author=Moreno Saiz, J.C. |date=2006 |title=''Senecio alboranicus'' |volume=2006 |article-number=e.T61626A12526844 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2006.RLTS.T61626A12526844.en |access-date=16 November 2021}} and {{convert|600|m|yd}} by {{convert|265|m|yd}} of [[Volcano|volcanic]] [[Extrusive|extrusion]] situated {{convert|48|km|mi}} from the port of Adra, [[Almería]] on the [[Spain|Spanish]] coast and {{convert|39|km|mi}} from the [[Melilla]] on the [[Africa]]n coast{{cite web | url = http://www.andalucia.com/environment/protect/alboran.htm | title = Alborán Natural Area | access-date = 2008-02-29 | work = Natural Parks - Almeria Province | publisher = Andalucia Com SL }} (previously [[Morocco]]). ''S. alboranicus'' is one of the 26 plants, 20 [[vascular plant]]s and 6 [[lichen]] cited as having inhabited the island, although, not all at the same time.{{cite web | url = http://www.ayto-gijon.es/documentos/jba/Actividades/congreso/Union%20Pdf/La%20conserv%20de%20la%20flora%20en%20Albor%E1n_Juan%20F%20Mota.pdf | title = Diapositiva 1 | access-date = 2008-02-29 | author = Juan F. Mota | author-link = Universidad de Almería | author2 = M.Encarna Merlo | author3 = Ana J. Sola | author4 = M.Luisa Jiménez-Sánchez et Joaquín Valero |name-list-style=amp | publisher = [[Gijón]] City Council | language = es }} [[Image:Range of Senecio alboranicus-Native.svg|thumb|200px|Range of ''S. alboranicus'' on 7.1 hectares]] :Typical of the tenacious genus ''Senecio'', the small shrub Azuzón de Alborán colonizes areas that could be described as disturbed and unstabilized as it does live where there is an accumulation of volcanic ashes and shell laden sand, historically perturbed by natural events and human activities. Also typical, this species produces three generations of plants each year and is non-competitive; the middle generation of ''S. alboranicus'' shares its part of the island with ''[[Lavatera mauritanica]]'' and ''[[Anacyclus alboranensis]]''. Atypical of the genus, this species is a [[halophile]], growing in soils with a known high concentration of salt.{{cite book |author1=Juan F. Mota | author-link = Universidad de Almería |author2=Antonio Mendoza |author3=Juan A. Garrido-Becerra |author4=Fabián Martínez-Hernández |author5=Ana J. Sola |author6=Joaquín Valero |author7=M. Luisa Jiménez-Sánchez | title = Capitulo VIII Tapiz viviente: La vegetación terrestre | url = http://www.juntadeandalucia.es/medioambiente/web/Bloques_Tematicos/Patrimonio_Natural._Uso_Y_Gestion/Espacios_Protegidos/Parajes_Naturales/Paraje_Natural_Isla_Alboran/VIII_la_vegetacion_terrestre.pdf | access-date = 2008-02-29 | language = es | isbn = 978-84-96329-92-8 }} :Azuzón de Alborán can be found growing at altitudes between 0 and {{convert|15|m|ft}}. The restricted size of the island and the rarity of the habitat make azuzón de Alborán particularly vulnerable to changes. Climatic conditions (quantity and distribution of rain, [[soil salinity]], etc.) and human activities (the lighthouse was once staffed); there have been large fluctuations in the numbers of individuals each year. These fluctuations affect not only the number of individual plants but also their size and the number of flowers. The decline of this species could be caused by alterations generated by human presence (military occupancy, artificial environments, etc.) in addition to events like natural changes or biotic threats (competition, parasitism, diseases, etc.), alterations which probably not coincidentally describe many of the conditions that occurred from the mapping those years. :Isla de Alborán is a [[protected area]], a [[marine park]] and an [[Important Ecological Areas|important ecological area]] for the [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]] and is especially protected by the [[Barcelona Convention]].{{cite web | url = http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=CELEX:31997R0338:EN:HTML | title = Council Regulation (EC) No 338/97 | access-date = 2008-02-29 | author = Barcelona Convention | author-link = Barcelona Convention | date = 1997-03-03 | work = Official Journal L 061 | pages = 0001–0069 }} Azuzón de Alborán is listed in Appendix I{{cite web | url = http://conventions.coe.int/Treaty/FR/Treaties/Html/104-1.htm | title = APPENDIX I / ANNEXE I | access-date = 2008-02-29 | author = Council of Europe | author-link = Council of Europe | date = 2002-03-01 | work = [[Convention on the Conservation of European Wildlife and Natural Habitats]] | archive-date = 2001-02-10 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20010210205630/http://conventions.coe.int/treaty/FR/Treaties/Html/104-1.htm | url-status = dead }} of [[Convention on the Conservation of European Wildlife and Natural Habitats|Bern Convention]].
